para.text: A new 3D element is the surface. A surface is defined by a set of data giving the height of the surface measured on grid points that are arranged in a 2-dimensional array. The surface definition in XYGRAPH3D also contains the x and y co-ordinates of these grid points.

para.text: can plot two parameters as a function of x and y simultaneously; one is plotted as a height value (z) giving a 3D image, the other as a colour by which individual elements are coloured. Both parameters are loaded as surfaces.

para.text: The surface is composed of small rectangular elements (cells) defined by four points (the corners). These cells need not to be flat; in extreme cases they can be heavily warped (as in the example of the pyramid). This can give problems in drawing and other processing. To compensate this these rectangular cells can be split into two or four triangular cells that by definition are always flat. This can be set by

para.text: If the cells are not split the following will occur:

para.text: - lighting (contour style 4, surface style 6) is calculated according to the average slope of the cell;
